DRE-9229 portico: main's infra test passes again — the DRE-8954 proof record is marked as a historical record, so the config files it quotes from other repos are not read as portico's

**What's wrong.** Portico main has been red since 11-05 1:58 AM PT: nightly CI run 42003663947 on becffebcd fails `infra/test/account_roster_in_docs.test.ts` ("no doc names a config file that does not exist"). The doc that trips it is `docs/parts-check-portico-proof-2026-11.md`, the [DRE-8954](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-8954/proof-real-portico-pull-requests-run-through-the-duplicate-check-after) proof record merged 11-04 7:23 AM PT. On lines 17, 31 and 35 it names `config/parts-count.json` and `config/repo-map.json`, which live in agent-bureau and bureau-pipeline, not in portico. The automatic red-main repair can't help, because portico's Red-Main Repair fails before it starts ([DRE-9228](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-9228/portico-the-red-main-repair-stub-grants-id-token-write-so-a-red-main)). **Acceptance criteria** - ☐ `docs/parts-check-portico-proof-2026-11.md` carries the test's own historical-record marker (`> **HISTORICAL RECORD`, within its first 30 lines, in the form the test already accepts). Alternatively, each of those paths names its repo so the test no longer reads it as a portico path. The PR says which, quoting the test's rule. - ☐ `infra/test/account_roster_in_docs.test.ts` passes on the branch, unchanged. The PR quotes it passing. - ☐ Nothing else in the proof record's findings changes. **Out of scope:** the Red-Main Repair stub ([DRE-9228](https://linear.app/dreadnoughtfoundry/issue/DRE-9228/portico-the-red-main-repair-stub-grants-id-token-write-so-a-red-main)), and why the original PR's push CI didn't run this shard.

DRE-8954 PROOF: real Portico pull requests run through the duplicate check after its count filed the cleanup cards, none failed by an untouched copy, and the roster reading names every repo

This card observes the duplicate-parts check working on real state in Portico, after the seven cards before it are done. It checks four things: * Portico's declaration landed before its stub, and the one-time count ran and filed its cleanup cards before the stub merged, and those cards are on the board. * Real Portico pull requests opened after the stub went live were run through the check, and none was failed by an existing copy it did not touch. * The atoms record carries the critic's provisional form, on a green `main`. * The roster reading ran over every roster repo. Every reading but one is a GitHub read made as the proof-reader identity, inside this organization: workflow runs, their jobs and logs through the Actions API, pull requests and their files, and file contents on a default branch or at a run's commit. The one other is the cleanup cards, read on Linear through `linear_ops.py description` and `state-of`, the reads the proof brief allows, inside its request cap. bureau-pipeline's runs are in this organization and public. The tagged lines it quotes — `parts-check:`, `parts-count:` and `parts-cleanup:` — are declared in bureau-pipeline's `config/proof-reach.json`. It makes no portal reading and no press, so the record's first line says that it read GitHub and those Linear cards only, and names the Portico commit the stub merged at. Observe after: the first Portico pull request opened after the Parts Check stub merges **Files:** docs/parts-check-portico-proof-2026-11.md ## Acceptance criteria - ☐ Portico's default branch carries `.github/bureau/design-system.json` naming the four folders `client/app/src/components/atoms`, `molecules`, `organisms` and `templates`. It carries `.github/workflows/parts-check.yml`, whose job `call` uses `dreadnought-foundry/bureau-pipeline/.github/workflows/parts-check.yml@stable` and grants only `contents: read`. And `.github/workflows/merge-gate.yml` names `Parts Check` in the list of workflows its `workflow_run` trigger watches. The record quotes those lines and the commits that added the declaration and the stub, with their merge times in PT, the declaration's earlier than the stub's. - ☐ A bureau-pipeline `Parts Count` run on `main`, event `push`, whose log carries `parts-count: portico — …`, concluded `success` before Portico's stub pull request merged. The record quotes that run's `parts-count: portico — …` line and its `parts-cleanup: portico — copy(ies), filed, already filed` line, with `` plus `` equal to ``. It lists each card id the run's `parts-cleanup: filed …` and `parts-cleanup: already filed …` lines name for Portico, gives the run's completion time and the stub's merge time in PT, and shows that the stub pull request's body names that same run's URL. - ☐ Every card id that run's Portico `parts-cleanup: filed …` and `parts-cleanup: already filed …` lines name is on the board as that copy's cleanup card. Read as the proof run with `linear_ops.py description `, its description carries the line `parts-copy: portico | | ` (read through the escapes a Linear round trip can add, a backslash before an underscore or the line set in backticks) for the part and copy path the run's count named; `linear_ops.py state-of ` answers its lane, and the record names it. The record also quotes Portico's entry in bureau-pipeline's `config/parts-count.json`, read through the contents API at that run's head commit, carrying `"agent": "agent:frontend"` and `"initiative": "initiative:foundry"`: the labels the run filed those cards with, beside `repo:portico`. The cards' own labels are not read, and the record says why: the proof run's Linear reads print labels only for an epic's children, and a cleanup card is filed in `Intake` with no parent. - ☐ At least one Portico pull request opened after the stub merged, other than the stub's own, has a `Parts Check` workflow run on its head whose `call / Parts check` job completed. The record names the pull request, the run and the job's conclusion, and quotes the job's `parts-check:` status line. - ☐ For every Portico pull request with a `Parts Check` run opened from the stub's merge to the time of the reading, the first ten at most, no `parts-check: COPY …` line names a copy whose copy declaration is not on a line that pull request's own diff adds, read from its files' patches. The record lists each such pull request with its job's conclusion and status line. So an existing copy the pull request did not touch failed none of them. - ☐ Portico's default branch `client/app/src/components/atoms/atoms.approved.test.ts` defines the `Provisional` entry form with exactly `line`, `card` and `approvedOn`, and no `permanentOn`. The `CI` run on Portico's `main` at the commit that added it concluded `success`. The record quotes the type and names the run. - ☐ A bureau-pipeline `Parts Roster` run on `main`, event `push`, at the merge commit of the card that added the workflow or later, concluded `success`, and has one `Read ` job for each key of `config/repo-map.json` at that run's commit. Each job concluded `success`, including the legs for a repo the App token could not reach. The record names the run and its conclusion, lists every job with its conclusion read through the Actions API, and names any key with no job and any job that did not conclude `success`. A leg for a repo the token could not reach is green by design, so a red leg or run is a defect in the workflow, not an unreachable repo. The repo-by-repo readings and their skip reasons are the follow-on rollout epic's to quote (DRE-8955). **Blocked by:** DRE-8947, DRE-8948, DRE-8949, DRE-8950, DRE-8951, DRE-8952, DRE-8953 — because the proof observes all of their work running live

On GitHub Team and Free, enabling Pages on a private repository serves the site **publicly**, and `gh-pages` holds a build for every open pull request — so the one-time operator step (**Settings → Pages → Deploy from a branch → `gh-pages` / (root)**) publishes all of them to anyone with the URL.
```text
VERDICT (held): REQUEST_CHANGES cause:unmet-criteria

## Summary
This change adds a short "historical record" notice to a finished proof write-up so that the project's automated document check stops flagging it. It does what the card asked, and the check now passes.

The only thing holding it back is paperwork. Every pull request must carry a one-sentence "What's new" line in its description, saying what kind of change it is and who it matters to, or saying "none". This one has no such line, so the release notes cannot be built from it. The fix is one sentence in the description and has nothing to do with the work itself.

## For the fixing agent
1. **Missing `What's new:` line (blocking, check 1, cause unmet-criteria; `standards/whats-new.md`).** The body snapshot, re-read just before this verdict, contains no line starting `What's new:` (`gh pr view 1107 --json body -q .body | grep -i "what's new"` printed nothing). For a docs-only record change the line is `What's new: none`. Fix it in the pull request BODY, not the diff. Edit the body, then push one empty commit to the same branch (`git commit --allow-empty -m "chore(DRE-9229): record the What's new line"`; DRE-5632). Do not touch the document.

Everything else I checked holds:
- The diff is 5 added lines in `docs/parts-check-portico-proof-2026-11.md`. The banner is at line 3, inside the first 30 lines, and matches `^>\s*\*\*(HISTORICAL RECORD|RETIRED|SUPERSEDED)\b`.
- I ran `npx tsx --test test/account_roster_in_docs.test.ts` in `infra/` on this branch: `# tests 4`, `# pass 4`, `# fail 0`. The test file is unchanged (the diff against `origin/main` is only the proof record).
- No TDD concern: the commit is docs only, and the test was already red on main.
- Scope is exactly the card. The banner text is accurate, since `parts-count.json` and `repo-map.json` are bureau-pipeline files. No code, test, or convention findings.

Once the body line is added, I would approve.
```
